title: GraphEdit zoom/pan is O(n^2) in node count. causing laggy/stuttery zoom feel
body:
### Tested versions

Godot 4.7.1-stable

### System information

Windows 10, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070, Compatibility (OpenGL 3.3) renderer.

### Issue description

Symptom: When using a large number of nodes in GraphEdit, for example 600, scroll-wheel zooming becomes extremely laggy, at roughly 280 ms per frame.
Expected: Smooth zooming.
Additional information: Based on inference, the call chain behavior in `scene/gui/graph_edit.cpp` is as follows:
1. During zoom/pan, `_update_scroll_offset()` is deferred, and it iterates over all GraphElement child nodes, calling `set_position()` and `set_scale()` on each node.
2. Each `set_scale()` synchronously triggers that node's `item_rect_changed` signal.
3. That signal is connected to `_graph_node_rect_changed()`, which unconditionally executes `callable_mp(...).call_deferred(_update_top_connection_layer)` for every node.
4. The first line of each deferred callback in turn calls `_update_scrollbars()`, which again iterates over all nodes to compute the canvas bounding box.
Therefore, n nodes produce n deferred callbacks, and each callback performs another O(n) full traversal, resulting in an overall complexity of O(n²).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached Minimal Reproduction Project (MRP) and run the game directly.
2. On the GraphEdit canvas in the running game, scroll the mouse wheel directly.
3. Observe the obvious lag on each zoom.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mrp_graph_edit_zoom.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32294668/mrp_graph_edit_zoom.zip)
